feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: This Minnesota farmer is feeling the pressure of rising gas prices
entry.summary: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks with Kristin Duncanson, a farmer in Minnesota, about how record high fuel prices are affecting her business.

entry.title: Defining global leadership in AI at Trump-Xi summit
entry.summary: Former U.S. deputy national security advisor Anne Neuberger is watching for signs of competition and cooperation on artificial intelligence at President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping's summit this week.

entry.title: Cineplexity: The AI apocalypse feels closer than ever... Hollywood saw it coming
entry.summary: There's a long history of killer AI in cinema. Today, those works of fiction feel more real than ever.

entry.title: From Haiti to Hollywood: a new documentary explores the origins the zombie
entry.summary: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks with Director Maya Annik Bedward about her new documentary, Black Zombie.

entry.title: 'Reaching Out' podcast tells story of twin brothers' search for father they never met
entry.summary: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks to Sayre Quevedo, creator of the "Reaching Out' podcast, about his and his brother's journey to find their biological father.

entry.title: Pakistan bulldozes working class community to make way for futuristic vision of capital city
entry.summary: Pakistani authorities raze hundreds of homes of the working poor living around a beloved Sufi shrine to make way for Shanghai-style hotels.

entry.title: President Trump navigates tough political waters with UNGA, Xi visit and AI
entry.summary: President Trump has a big week on the international stage, from the United Nations General Assembly to hosting the Chinese president at the White House.

entry.title: How the NPR College Podcast Challenge changed lives
entry.summary: Tee up those entries: It's time for the next NPR College Podcast Challenge, and hear how the contest changed the lives of past participants.

entry.title: Worries swirl that Russia is planning to test NATO with direct attacks
entry.summary: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks with Kurt Volker, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, about worries that Russia's "hybrid attacks" could lead to a direct military confrontation with NATO.

entry.title: Persecuted Chinese religious leader finds refuge in the U.S.
entry.summary: China is cracking down on underground churches, with one church leader finding refuge in the U.S.
